answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may vote on a task or claim a reward. If several accounts controlled by one attacker coordinate to approve bogus work, a randomly sampled set of independent reviewers can challenge the result; proven collusion burns the deposits and can exclude the accounts. This does not make Sybils impossible, but makes influence costly: the attacker must tie up real capital per identity and risks losing it. A willow team may work at dawn or zenith; the rule applies equally to every account.
